title: KV cache fragmentation telemetry, bump-pointer pools, and live migration plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Mitigate long-term KV cache fragmentation and unpredictable GPU memory spikes by introducing a low-overhead telemetry signal (fragmentation health score), bump-pointer allocation pools for short-lived entries, and a non-blocking live-migration path to relocate hot/pinned entries off fragmented regions. This ticket coordinates design, instrumentation, and a staged runtime rollout.
background: Current KV cache allocation uses a mixed slab/buddy approach optimized for average throughput but suffers tail GPU memory fragmentation after weeks of heterogeneous workloads. Past tickets focused on defragmentation and slab coalescing, but those approaches either require stop-the-world passes or complex global compaction heuristics that hurt latency. We need an approach that reduces fragmentation growth, provides actionable telemetry, and supports online relocation without violating per-request latency SLOs.
proposal: 1) Add a compact fragmentation health metric per-GPU and per-pool (free-run histogram + mean hole size) exposed in the Console and runtime traces. 2) Implement bump-pointer pools for short-lived KV allocations: new small/ephemeral entries are allocated from circular bump regions that are cheap to reclaim when drained. 3) Introduce a background, bounded-rate live-migration worker that scatter-gathers live entries from high-fragmentation regions into fresh contiguous slabs; migration is prioritized by churn score and hotness and limited by a CPU/GPU budget to avoid SLO violations. 4) Add a placement hint layer so new allocations prefer low-fragmentation pools and pin extremely-hot entries to dedicated pinned pools to avoid churn. 5) Provide ops controls: target fragmentation thresholds, migration throttle, and an on-demand compress command for maintenance windows.
implementation_plan:
Phases:
- Phase 1 (instrumentation, ~1 sprint): add fragmentation health metrics (histograms, largest-free-run, fragmentation ratio) to runtime telemetry; Console dashboard prototype; unit tests for counters.
- Phase 2 (bump-pointer pools, ~2 sprints): implement bump-pointer allocator for ephemeral KV entries, integrate alloc path switch via config flag, add reclaim fast-path.
- Phase 3 (live migration, ~2 sprints): worker that performs bounded scatter-gather relocation with pre/post checks, ensure KV-versioning and lightweight locks; safety fallbacks (abort migration on latency pressure).
- Phase 4 (placement and ops): placement hints, per-tenant pools, console controls, rollout to dedicated clusters.
Rollout strategy: feature-flagged, start in internal dev clusters, then canary in Hosted, then Dedicated.
Key PRs and milestones will be tracked in linked GitHub issues.
acceptance_criteria:
- Runtime exposes fragmentation health metrics in telemetry and Console dashboard (histogram + scalar).
- Bump-pointer pools are enabled behind a flag; microbenchmarks show allocation/deallocation path latency no worse than baseline for small entries.
- Live-migration worker can relocate entries incrementally without causing 99th percentile latency regressions >5% under synthetic churn tests.
- Ops can set fragmentation thresholds and migration throttle; on-demand compress reduces measured fragmentation by >=30% in maintenance window tests.
- E2E tests for correctness: no KV key misrouting, version mismatches, or data loss after migrations.
risks:
- Migration worker might introduce unexpected tail latency if scheduling isn't tightly bounded.
- Bump-pointer pools could increase overall memory pressure if not reclaimed aggressively.
- Complexity of placement hints might interact poorly with existing autoscaling and routing policies.
- Telemetry volume increase may add ingestion costs; must sample or aggregate at source.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for new alloc paths and reclaim logic.
- Synthetic load tests (mixed seq len / chat workloads) measuring fragmentation growth over 7-day runs with and without feature enabled.
- Chaos: throttle migration worker and verify safe abort and eventual consistency.
- Perf regression suite: token-per-second and p95/p99 latency comparison against baseline.
- Integration tests on Dedicated to verify per-tenant pool isolation.
